messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — eu-west GPU pool has been showing a slow 'queue creep' for ~3h. Not a spike but steady growth: p95/p99 latencies are inching up and avg batch size is drifting higher.

Jon: Did the pager go out?

sre-bot: ALERT (eu-west/gpu-queue): queue_depth > 120 for 10m — 1 warning (no critical). Triggered 3x in the last 24h.

Maya: Alert was debounced. Pulled the dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/eu-west/d/queue-ops/queue-overview

Ana: Can you paste the Prometheus queries you used to eyeball batch size vs inflight?

Maya: Sure — I used an ad-hoc to compute avg batch size by instance: 

```
(sum by (instance) (rate(gpu_inflight_requests_total[5m]))) / (sum by (instance) (rate(gpu_dispatched_batches_total[5m])))
```

Maya: And per-model qps for the region: 

```
sum by (model) (rate(requests_total{region="eu-west"}[5m]))
```

Kevin: I also saw a bump in network retransmits on a subset of nodes during the same timeframe. Stalled RPCs would cause inflight requests to pile up and delay autoscaler reactions.

Jon: Important question — is this autoscaler tuning or a transient network hiccup? Our autoscaler policy triggers when queue_avg_5m > 100 with a 6m cooldown. For slow creep that might be too conservative.

Ana: Also consider scale_step and cooldown together. If the step is small (1-2 pods) and queue keeps growing you get repeated small scales -> cost churn.

Kevin: Cost note: eu-west burst capacity is pricier (~1.6x). If we overshoot frequently we'll see a material bill increase. Prefer faster scaling but with burst caps keyed to customer tags.

Jon: Proposal: add a recording rule that surfaces per-zone queue_derivative to catch slow growth. Example: 

```
- record: infra:queue_derivative:5m
  expr: increase(gpu_queue_size[5m]) / 300
```

Jon: Then alert on derivative > 0.5 req/s sustained for 15m. That should catch 'creep' earlier than absolute queue thresholds.

Maya: Good idea. Also want a per-model batch-size heatmap on the queue dashboard so we can pinpoint which model's traffic pattern is inflating batches.

Ana: I can prototype a heatmap panel and add a per-model QPS row to the queue dashboard to make that correlation quick.

Kevin: On the infra side I grabbed kube-proxy logs showing `grpc: read tcp ... reset by peer` around 02:14Z which aligns with the earliest creep start.

```
[kube-proxy] 2024-06-12T02:14:21Z ERROR rpc: stream error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
```

Maya: Action items: 
- Jon: create prometheus recording rule + alert PR (assign eng-infra)
- Ana: add heatmap + per-model qps row to queue dashboard (assign eng-platform)
- Kevin: run targeted synthetic repro on canary region and capture network metrics (assign eng-infra)
- Maya: short-term runbook tweak: reduce eu-west cooldown to 3m and allow scale_step up to 4 during high-derivative windows

Jon: I'll draft the PR. Paging policy question: page on derivative immediately, or only after it persists? I propose page only if derivative persists >20m to reduce noise.

Ana: Agree — low-noise initial behavior. Page to oncall only after persistence window.

sre-bot: NOTE: incident stub INC-2024-322 created with links to grafana and logs.

Kevin: Cost estimate: if we add 4 extra nodes for ~40m in eu-west it's ~€220. I'll tag the synthetic run resources with customer:billing to confirm environment.

Jon: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-monitoring/pull/842 — recording rule + alert, basic tests green.

Ana: Dashboard PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-dashboards/pull/129 — added heatmap and per-model qps row.

Kevin: Starting canary synthetic load: `loadtester --region eu-west-canary --model small-embed --ramp 0.2qps/min --duration 60m` — will stream traces to the infra bucket.

Maya: We'll monitor the derivative panel and adjust runbook/paging if it fires. If repro confirms network blips, escalate to cloud networking. Thanks all :thumbsup:
